newsitem.title: USA: PP&L seeks to sell power throughout state.
newsitem.headline: PP&L seeks to sell power throughout state.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co filed an application Wednesday with the state's Public Utility Commission to sell electricity and related services throughout Pennsylvania, the utility said Thursday.

The license would allow the PP&L Resources Inc subsidiary to sell electricity and related services outside of its current 29-county service territory in the central and eastern part of the Keystone State, it explained.
The competitive selling of electricity could begin as early as this summer with customer choice pilot programs throughout Pennsylvania, it noted.

Under state law, any company -- including electric utilities -- need to apply for a PUC license to sell electricity in the new competitive market. Review of the application is expected to take about 45 days.

"With the advent of customer choice in Pennsylvania, PP&L intends to sell generation priced at competitive market levels to customers throughout the commonwealth," said John Sipics, PP&L's vice president of Retail Energy Supply. "We're confident that PP&L will be very competitive in the Pennsylvania marketplace."
Along with selling electric energy and capacity, PP&L said, it intends to sell such related services to customers as energy efficiency, energy auditing and energy consulting.
